Plan section 2.5 / 12 and the README env table say VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY must never be committed, but packages/server/data/vapid-keys.json is git-tracked and contains a live private key (written by the file fallback in packages/server/src/push/vapid.ts, then accidentally committed). packages/server/.test-db.sqlite is also a tracked test artifact.

Fix:
1. git rm --cached packages/server/data/vapid-keys.json packages/server/.test-db.sqlite
2. Add both paths to .gitignore (root or packages/server/.gitignore)
3. Treat the committed key as compromised: generate a fresh pair (npx web-push generate-vapid-keys) for production, delivered via VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY / VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY env vars (sealed secret work tracked separately in bf-4012 - mention rotation there via comment)
4. Keep vapid.ts behavior (env-first, generated file fallback for local dev only)
5. Add a short note to docs/security.md documenting the rotation and that clients subscribed under the old key must re-subscribe

Acceptance criteria:
- git ls-files shows neither packages/server/data/vapid-keys.json nor packages/server/.test-db.sqlite
- .gitignore covers both paths; local dev still works (file regenerated at startup when env vars absent)
- docs/security.md notes the key rotation
issue.title: Remove committed VAPID private key from git and rotate keys

issue.description:
## Evidence
docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) states as Context: "deployments/prometheus/alerts.yml has no rule for FailedMount/pod-not-ready conditions, only up{job=\"mta-my-way\"} == 0, which a pod that never starts scraping won't reliably trigger. It went undetected for 9+ hours until this audit." ADR-001's own "Follow-up work" list says alerting for this was "filed as beads" alongside three other items — one of those three (pinning the image off :latest) really was filed and closed as bf-26ijn, but this alerting item was not: no open, closed, or blocked bead in this workspace mentions FailedMount, pod-not-ready, or ContainerCreating detection (confirmed via bf list --json search across all 390 beads; the only hit is bf-2uz2z, which is the incident triage itself, not a prevention/detection fix).

Current state of deployments/prometheus/alerts.yml (read in full): it has MtaMyWayHighErrorRate, MtaMyWayHighLatency, MtaMyWayServiceDown (up{job=...}==0), feed/push/cache/trip/equipment rules — nothing keyed on kube_pod_status_phase, kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason="ContainerCreating"}, or CSI FailedMount events. A pod stuck in ContainerCreating never emits the `up` metric at all (nothing is scraping it), so MtaMyWayServiceDown cannot catch this failure mode — exactly the blind spot that let the actual incident run 10+ hours.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Add a Prometheus alert rule (in deployments/prometheus/alerts.yml, or the equivalent cluster-level rule if kube-state-metrics rules live in declarative-config instead — check both) that fires when the mta-my-way pod is not Ready / stuck in ContainerCreating for more than e.g. 10-15 minutes, using kube_pod_status_ready / kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason from kube-state-metrics (available on apexalgo-iad per other cluster monitoring)
- Alert severity should be critical (this is the same class as MtaMyWayServiceDown but catches the case where the service never starts scraping)
- If kube-state-metrics rules must live in a different repo/location (e.g. jedarden/declarative-config alongside the cluster's Prometheus config) rather than this repo's deployments/prometheus/alerts.yml, document that split clearly and file/point to the actual location
- No live cluster changes required to file or write this rule — it's a manifest/config change; applying it to the live Prometheus instance goes through the normal declarative-config + ArgoCD path per workspace policy
issue.title: Add Prometheus alert for pod not-Ready / FailedMount conditions (ADR-001 detection gap)

issue.description:
## Goal
Proactively inform commuters about disruptions to their specific stations and lines, and help them respond. Alert text is simplified from MTA's confusing language into plain English.

## Why This Matters
The competitive analysis documents that MTA notifications are either too broad (line-level) or incomprehensible (raw MTA alert text). This is a key differentiator.

## Key Decisions
- Template-based alert rewriter with ~15 regex patterns covering recurring MTA alert formats
- Graceful fallback: unmatched alerts shown as raw text with "raw alert" indicator
- Web Push API (RFC 8030) with VAPID authentication for push notifications
- Push subscriptions keyed by endpoint hash — no user accounts needed
- Quiet hours (default midnight to 5 AM)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Alerts feed parsed and simplified into plain language (target: 85%+ match rate)
- Filtered alerts displayed in app, scoped to user's favorites
- Web Push notifications delivered for severe alerts
- Trip replacement period detection shows cancelled trips

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 1 backend (alert feed polling) and Phase 2 (commute configuration for filtering)
issue.title: Phase 3: Alerts & Notifications — Service Alerts, Push

Extracted complete /api/health endpoint behavior from app.ts lines 874-1129. 

KEY FINDINGS:

Query Validation:
- Uses emptyQuerySchema (z.object({}).strict())
- Accepts NO query parameters - ANY query params cause 400 error
- Error response: { error: 'validation failed', details: [...] }

HTTP Status Codes:
- 200: Fewer than 3 feeds failing (consecutiveFailures > 0, had prior success, last success > 5min ago)
- 503: 3+ feeds meet failing criteria
- Note: 'degraded' status can coexist with 200 (e.g., one stale feed but <3 failing)

Response Fields:
- status: 'ok' | 'degraded' (ok = all feeds ok AND alerts ok)
- timestamp: ISO 8601
- uptime_seconds: since SERVER_START_MS
- deploymentMode: 'core-only' | 'full'
- feeds: Array of feed states with per-feed status (circuit_open | never_polled | stale | ok)
- alerts: alerts polling subsystem status
- delayDetector: delay detector subsystem status
- delayPredictor: delay predictor subsystem status
- equipment: elevator/escalator outage status
- pushDb: { ready, subscriptionCount }
- statefulSubsystem: stateful subsystem status
- cacheHitRate: fraction 0-1
- memory: Node.js process memory snapshot
- failingFeedsCount: count of feeds failing >5 minutes

Found from declarative-config bead declarat-35a63e40 (ArgoCD triage follow-ups). The mta-my-way-ns-apexalgo-iad app has been Degraded with two root causes in this repo's artifacts:

1. IMAGE: ronaldraygun/mta-my-way:0.0.82 (pinned in declarative-config deployment-core.yaml / deployment-stateful.yaml) is unpullable on apexalgo-iad despite the docker-hub-registry pull secret being attached — ImagePullBackOff persists, so the tag appears to be missing from Docker Hub. Either push 0.0.82 (VERSION file + container-build flow) or bump to the newest tag that exists and update declarative-config to match.

2. SEALED SECRET: SealedSecret mta-my-way-secrets fails 'no key could decrypt secret (vapid-public-key)' — the ciphertext was sealed with a key that predates the cluster's current sealed-secrets key. Needs re-sealing against the live key: take the vapid public key plaintext, kubeseal against apexalgo-iad, and replace sealedsecret.yaml in declarative-config (see sealedsecret-template.yaml there for the field list).

Also noted by triage (declarative-config side, may fix there): Deployments are shared with a legacy ArgoCD app named 'mta-my-way' (SharedResourceWarning) — the declarative-config manifests application.yaml.disabled may be the leftover definition.
issue.notes: Verified the incident was remediated concurrently; no duplicate commit created. declarative-config commit 0b8c8a6b resealed vapid-public-key. kubeseal validation against apexalgo-iad's sealed-secrets-apexalgo-iad controller succeeds, and live SealedSecret mta-my-way-secrets reports Synced=True with both VAPID keys. Recovery workflow mta-my-way-recovery-082-42nw2 succeeded at 2026-08-22T06:50:21Z; pods have pulled ronaldraygun/mta-my-way:0.0.82 (digest sha256:3205f0edb757eeab5aee84501e59b8a0167442f786aa277622032944427c4093) and current events show restarts rather than ImagePullBackOff. application.yaml.disabled remains disabled. Separate follow-up: the pulled containers are CrashLoopBackOff and the stateful pod is ContainerCreating, a runtime issue outside these two blockers.
issue.title: Prod deploy blockers from ArgoCD triage: 0.0.82 image unpullable on Docker Hub + vapid-public-key needs re-seal

issue.close_reason:
Security headers already fully implemented with comprehensive protection:

1. Content-Security-Policy (CSP) - restricts sources for scripts, styles, images, fonts, workers, etc.
2. X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff - prevents MIME type sniffing attacks
3. X-Frame-Options: DENY - prevents clickjacking
4. Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin - controls referrer information leakage
5. Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) - max-age=31536000 with includeSubDomains and preload (HTTPS only)
6. Permissions-Policy - blocks geolocation, camera, microphone, payment, and other sensitive APIs
7. Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin - prevents window.opener access
8. Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin - restricts cross-origin resource access
9. Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp - requires COOP/COEP for certain features
10. X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block - legacy XSS protection

All 17 unit tests pass. Middleware is applied globally in app.ts and includes configuration options for CSP/HSTS toggles and custom policies.
issue.description: Implement security headers including CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, and others to protect against common browser-based vulnerabilities.
issue.title: Add secure headers

## What
Implement the security model: Cloudflare WAF rules, Hono rate limiting middleware, Zod input validation, CSP headers.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Cloudflare WAF: rate-limit rule for /api/* at 100 req/min per IP (configure in tunnel dashboard)
- [ ] Hono middleware: in-memory token bucket rate limiter (60 req/min per IP)
- [ ] Zod schemas for all API inputs: push subscription payload, commute analysis request
- [ ] Return 400 with structured error for invalid payloads
- [ ] CSP headers: default-src 'self', script-src 'self', style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'
- [ ] Security headers: X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy
- [ ] Trip share link TTL: 24h expiry enforced server-side
- [ ] Audit: verify no PII stored server-side (push subs keyed by hash, no user identity)

## Considerations
- In-memory rate limiter resets on pod restart — acceptable for single-container deployment
- Cloudflare WAF is the first line of defense; Hono middleware is the second
- Zod schemas should be shared with frontend for consistent validation
issue.title: Security: rate limiting, CSP, Zod validation

This is the entire value proposition of the app — "open and see your data in under 3 seconds." The home screen IS the app. Everything else is secondary to this screen working perfectly.

## Subtasks
- [ ] FavoriteCard component: station name, configured lines/direction, next 2-3 arrivals inline
- [ ] FavoritesList component: ordered list of FavoriteCards, drag-to-reorder
- [ ] ArrivalRow component: line bullet (official MTA color), destination, minutes away, confidence indicator
- [ ] ArrivalList component: grouped by direction (Uptown/Downtown with compass-aware labels)
- [ ] LineBullet component: circular, 32px, official MTA color, white/dark text
- [ ] ConfidenceBar component: solid (high), dashed (medium), dotted (low)
- [ ] HomeScreen: favorites list + "Updated Xs ago" indicator + pull-to-refresh
- [ ] StationScreen: full station detail with all arrivals, both directions, add-to-favorites button
- [ ] FavoriteEditor: configure lines and direction per favorite
- [ ] useArrivals hook: fetch arrivals for a station, auto-refresh every 30s, return DataState
- [ ] useFavorites hook: CRUD operations on favorites store
- [ ] Pull-to-refresh: trigger immediate API fetch, optional haptic on iOS
- [ ] DataState wrapper on all data views (loading skeleton, empty, error, stale, offline)

## Considerations
- Arrival time is the HERO number — 24px, 800 weight, the largest element on screen
- Line bullets must be 44px tap target (32px visible + padding)
- Direction labels should say "Uptown / Bronx-bound" not just "Northbound" — context matters
- Multi-complex stations (Times Square) show a link to the other platform group
- DataState skeleton should match the shape of the actual content (not a generic spinner)

issue.notes:
[migrated notes from bf-4cpi]
Implemented swipe gestures on FavoriteCard: swipe-left reveals delete action (red), swipe-right reveals edit action (MTA blue). Non-passive touchmove listener with 72px threshold and snap animation. Committed in 2f4c4f0.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Attaching the non-passive touchmove listener via useEffect (rather than React onTouchMove) lets us call preventDefault to suppress page scroll during horizontal swipes. Direction-lock heuristic (|deltaX| > |deltaY| * 1.2) prevents false triggers on diagonal scrolls.
- **What did not:** The initial bead run completed the implementation but exited with code 1 before closing, so the bead landed here as a retry. The code was already committed in 2f4c4f0.
- **Surprise:** FavoriteCard already had a partial action-panel scaffold (absolute-positioned edit/delete divs) from the initial component design — only the gesture state machine and non-passive DOM listener needed to be added.
- **Reusable pattern:** For swipe-to-reveal in React: (1) store touchStartX/Y in refs, (2) attach non-passive touchmove via useEffect with {passive:false}, (3) direction-lock on first move exceeding 5px, (4) clamp offset to +/-ACTION_WIDTH*1.3, (5) snap to +/-ACTION_WIDTH or 0 on touchend based on threshold.

## Analysis Complete

### 1. All Middleware Exported ✅
All 49 middleware modules are properly exported from middleware/index.ts. This requirement was already complete.

### 2. Fixed: Duplicate Middleware Removed
Found and removed duplicate massAssignmentProtection() on line 554 (was also on line 502). This was the only actual issue found.

### 3. Understanding '31 Unused Middleware'
The key finding: MOST of the 'unused' exports are NOT middleware handlers—they are helper/utility functions meant to be called by other code, NOT mounted as middleware.

**Helper Functions (NOT middleware, should NOT be mounted):**
- token-encryption.ts: Only utilities (encryptToken, decryptToken)
- jwt-validation.ts: Only utilities (validateJwt, verifyJwt)
- password-management.ts, audit-log.ts, auth-rate-limit.ts: All utilities
- captcha.ts, authorization-security.ts, enhanced-jwt-security.ts: All utilities
- concurrent-session-management.ts, suspicious-activity-notifications.ts: All utilities

**Actual Middleware Handlers (not mounted, but by design):**
- cookie-security.ts: csrfCookie, cookieSecurityValidator, cookieSessionAuth
  → App uses session token auth (optionalAuth + sessionSecurity) instead
- cache.ts: staticCache, semiStaticCache, realtimeCache, etc.
  → Already using custom cache headers per-route
- header-validation.ts: headerValidation, strictHeaderValidation
  → May be worth adding, but not critical

**Route-Specific Middleware (already used correctly inline):**
- requirePermission, requireRole, requireAdmin, requireResourceAccess
- auditLogAccess, requireOwnershipOrAdmin
- These are used per-route as needed, not global

### 4. Middleware Order is Correct
The current middleware order follows security best practices:
1. Request ID (correlation)
2. Security headers (CSP)
3. Security logging
4. HTTP method restrictions
5. Request smuggling protection
6. Response splitting protection
7. Host header protection
8. Tracing
9. Request size limits
10. Path traversal prevention
11. Input sanitization
12. SSRF protection
13. Content type validation
14. JSON depth protection
15. Mass assignment protection
16. Optional auth
17. Session security
18. CSRF protection
19. HPP protection
20. Open redirect protection
21. HTTP metrics
22. Rate limiting
23. Response size limits
24. Compression

### Conclusion
The security middleware integration is well-designed. The 'unused' middleware are primarily:
1. Helper functions (not middleware)
2. Alternative implementations not chosen for this architecture
3. Route-specific authorization middleware already used correctly

No additional middleware should be mounted—the current implementation is intentional and appropriate.

issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-4dutr, 2026-07-04T09:52:24.232519247Z, author cli]
## Module-Level Mutable State Audit — Complete Inventory

### Methodology
Scanned all `.ts` files in `packages/server/src/` (excluding tests, `dist/`, `__tests__/`, `.d.ts`) for module-level mutable containers: `Map`, `Set`, `[]`, `{}`, and mutable `let` singletons. Compared each against `cleanupAllState()` in `packages/server/src/integration/test-helpers.ts` (lines 445–501).

---

### COVERED by cleanupAllState() — 14 modules, fully reset

| Module | Mutable State | Reset Function Called |
|--------|--------------|----------------------|
| `cache.ts` | `feedStates` (Map), `arrivalsCache` (Map), `positionsCache` (Map) | `resetAllCacheStateForTesting` |
| `alerts-poller.ts` | `pollTimer`, `previousAlertIds` (Set), `changeListeners` (Array), `cache` object | `resetAlertsCacheForTesting` |
| `middleware/authentication.ts` | `apiKeys` (Map), `sessions` (Map), `auditLog` (Array), `refreshTokens` (Map), `deviceFingerprints` (Map), `oauthProviders` (Map), `oauthStates` (Map), `totpConfigs` (Map), `authFailuresByIp` (Map), `suspiciousIps` (Map) | `resetAuthenticationState` |
| `middleware/api-key-management.ts` | `API_KEY_REGISTRY` (Map), `API_KEY_LAST_USED` (Map), `API_KEY_DESCRIPTIONS` (Map) | `clearAllApiKeys` |
| `middleware/rate-limiter.ts` | `buckets` (Map) | `resetRateLimiter` |
| `middleware/auth-rate-limit.ts` | `rateLimitStore` (Map), `apiKeyRateLimitStore` (Map), `trustedIps` (Set), `unbannedIps` (Set) | `_clearAllRateLimits` |
| `middleware/authorization-security.ts` | `accessPatterns` (Map) | `clearAccessPatterns` |
| `middleware/audit-log.ts` | `AUDIT_LOG` (Array) | `resetAuditLog` |
| `middleware/token-encryption.ts` | `oldKeys` (Map) | `resetEncryptionState` |
| `trip-tracking.ts` | `db` (let), `stations` (let) | `resetTripTrackingForTesting` |
| `shuttle-matcher.ts` | `segments` (let) | `resetShuttleCache` |
| `delay-detector.ts` | `trackedTrips` (Map), `activePredictedAlerts` (Map), `alertListeners` (Array) | `resetDelayDetector` |
| `transformer.ts` | `prevTripStops` (Map) | `resetTransformerState` |
| `context-service.ts` | `db` (let), `stations` (let), `currentContext` (let), `currentSettings` (let) | `resetContextService` |

---

### GAP Category A — Has reset function but NOT called from cleanupAllState() — 9 modules

| Module | Mutable State | Existing Reset Function | Gap |
|--------|--------------|----------------------|-----|
| `delay-predictor.ts` | `delayRecords` (Array), `aggregatedStats` (Map), `weatherOverride`, `currentWeather`, `config`, `_travelTimes`, `stations` | `resetDelayPredictor()` exists, clears all | **Not called** from cleanupAllState |
| `middleware/captcha.ts` | `failedCaptchaAttempts` (Map), `captchaConfigs` (Map), `defaultCaptchaConfig` | `resetCaptchaTracking()` exists, clears all | **Not called** from cleanupAllState |
| `middleware/concurrent-session-management.ts` | `userSessionRegistry` (Map), `deviceSessionRegistry` (Map) | `clearAllSessions()` exists, clears all | **Not called** from cleanupAllState |
| `middleware/csrf-protection.ts` | `tokenStore` (Map) | `clearCsrfTokenStore()` exists, clears all | **Not called** from cleanupAllState |
| `middleware/dynamic-rbac-cache.ts` | `permissionCache` (Map), `permissionOverrides` (Map), `emergencyRevocations` (Set) | `clearCache()` only clears `permissionCache` — **incomplete even if called**. Must also call `clearPermissionOverrides()` + `clearEmergencyRevocations()` | **Not called** AND reset is incomplete |
| `middleware/jwt-validation.ts` | `replayStore` (Map) | `cleanupReplayStore()` only removes expired entries, not all | **Not called** AND reset is incomplete |
| `middleware/structured-audit-log.ts` | `auditLogStorage` (Array) | `clearAuditLogs()` exists, clears all | **Not called** from cleanupAllState |
| `middleware/suspicious-activity-notifications.ts` | `notificationPreferences` (Map), `recentEvents` (Map), `notificationHistory` (Map), `notificationRateLimits` (Map), `notificationTemplates` (Map) | `resetNotificationStorage()` exists, clears all | **Not called** from cleanupAllState |
| `routes/password-reset.routes.ts` | `users` (Map) | `clearAllUsers()` exists, clears all | **Not called** from cleanupAllState |

---

### GAP Category B — NO reset function exists at all — 8 modules

| Module | Mutable State (variable: type) | Risk |
|--------|-------------------------------|------|
| `equipment-poller.ts` | `pollTimer` (let), `equipmentByStation` (Map), `stationNameToIds` (Map) | Polling timer leaks across tests; stale equipment data |
| `middleware/enhanced-jwt-security.ts` | `tokenUsageRecords` (Map), `_deviceFingerprints` (Map), `tokenRevocations` (Map) | Only `clearOldTokenUsage(30)` for partial cleanup; no full reset. Leaked revocations/tokens persist across tests |
| `middleware/password-management.ts` | `passwordResetTokens` (Map), `passwordHistory` (Map), `passwordValidationAttempts` (Map), `passwordResetAttempts` (Map), `accountLockouts` (Map), `breachedPasswordCache` (Map) | Only per-key/per-email clear functions; no comprehensive reset. Lockouts and rate limits persist across tests |
| `middleware/session-security.ts` | `sessionSecurityEvents` (Map), `deviceTrustStorage` (Map) | Only per-session `clearSecurityEvents(id)`; no bulk reset. Device trust scores persist across tests |
| `middleware/enhanced-authorization.ts` | `RESOURCE_TYPES` (Map) — **mutated at runtime** via `.set()` on line 105 | Static-looking but actually modified; no reset. Custom resource types accumulate across tests |
| `push/briefing.ts` | `sentToday` (Set), `lastCheckDate` (string) | Briefing dedup state leaks; push notifications may be suppressed in subsequent tests |
| `transfer/travel-times.ts` | `travelTimesCache` (let, nullable object) | Cached travel times persist across tests |
| `trip-lookup.ts` | `tripFirstSeen` (Map) | Trip timestamps leak; "new trip" detection broken across tests |

---

### Not Gaps — Read-only constants (never mutated after init)

These are module-level Sets/Maps but are never `.set()`/`.add()`/`.delete()` after initialization:
- `middleware/http-request-smuggling.ts` → `STANDARD_HEADERS` (Set)
- `middleware/rbac.ts` → `ROLE_DEFINITIONS` (Map)
- `migration/sql-validator.ts` → `SQL_RESERVED_KEYWORDS` (Set)
- `observability/logger.ts` → `SENSITIVE_FIELDS` (Set)

---

### Summary

- **14 modules** fully covered
- **9 modules** have reset functions but are **not called** from `cleanupAllState()`
- **8 modules** have **no reset function at all**
- **4 "constants"** are read-only and don't need cleanup

**Total mutable-state containers:** ~70 across all modules
**Containers NOT reset between tests:** ~30+

### Additional Concern

The `try-catch` in `cleanupAllState()` silently swallows errors. If a module is `vi.mock()` in a test file (replacing its exports with stubs), the reset function won't exist on the mock and the cleanup is silently skipped. This means even the 14 "covered" modules can leak state if any test file mocks them. This is by design per the comment (lines 441-443) but is worth flagging as a structural risk — a future test author may not realize that mocking a module also opts it out of cleanup.
issue.title: Audit all module-level mutable state for test isolation gaps

issue.description:
## What
Build the core backend: Hono app that polls all 8 MTA GTFS-RT feeds every 30 seconds, parses protobuf (including NYCT extensions), transforms into StationArrivals model, and caches in memory.

## Why
This is the beating heart of the entire application. Every feature — arrivals, transfers, alerts, delay detection, trip tracking, train positions — depends on this pipeline running correctly every 30 seconds.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Hono app setup (app.ts): routes, middleware, static asset serving config
- [ ] Feed poller (poller.ts): setInterval(30s), fetch all 8 feeds in parallel with Promise.allSettled
- [ ] Feed parser (parser.ts): protobuf decode using compiled proto, extract NYCT extensions
- [ ] Feed transformer (transformer.ts): convert parsed data → StationArrivals indexed by stopId
- [ ] In-memory cache (cache.ts): 30s TTL, fallback to last-good response on fetch failure, mark stale after 5 min
- [ ] Circuit breaker: after 3 consecutive failures on a feed, pause 60s before retrying
- [ ] API routes: GET /api/arrivals/:stationId, GET /api/stations, GET /api/stations/:id
- [ ] Health endpoint: GET /api/health with per-feed status
- [ ] Structured JSON logging on every poll (timestamp, feed, status, latency, entities, errors)
- [ ] Static asset serving: Hono serves /* from web dist directory, /api/* from routes
- [ ] Entry point (index.ts): start server, start poller, log startup info

## Considerations
- Use Promise.allSettled (not Promise.all) so one feed failure doesn't block others
- Each feed has its own circuit breaker state — independent failure isolation
- The cache must serve stale data rather than nothing when feeds are down
- Per-feed timestamps must be tracked for the data freshness feature (Phase 7)
- Memory usage: ~8 feeds × ~500 entities × 30s = manageable in-memory, no external cache needed
- The poller should start polling immediately on startup (not wait 30s for first poll)
issue.title: Backend: feed poller, parser, transformer, cache

issue.close_reason: Already implemented in commit 8a8e8f77 (2026-08-20). Investigation confirmed: push subscriptions DB has lazy initialization with retry logic, degraded mode health reporting, and 503 responses for DB-dependent routes. issue.description:
Incremental first step toward ADR-001 (docs/plan/plan.md, ADR-001,
2026-07-20). Today the SQLite databases backing push subscriptions and
alert history are opened as part of server startup in
packages/server/src/index.ts (initPushDatabase in
packages/server/src/push/subscriptions.ts, plus the alert-history
equivalent). If the /data mount is present but the underlying
filesystem is unwritable or corrupt, this can take the whole process
down with it, even though nothing about arrivals, stations, routes,
alerts, or commute analysis needs that database.

Change: make these opens lazy (open on first use, with retry) and
non-fatal -- if the open fails, log the error, mark that subsystem
"degraded" in GET /api/health, and have the push/password-reset routes
return 503 instead of the process failing to start. Core routes
(/api/arrivals/*, /api/stations, /api/routes, /api/alerts,
/api/commute/analyze, static assets) must keep working regardless of
push/alert-history DB state.

Note: this does not fix the class of outage found live on 2026-07-20
(a Kubernetes-level FailedMount that blocks the container from
starting at all, before any Node.js code runs) -- that requires the
deployment-topology split described in ADR-001. This bead is the
in-app defense-in-depth half of that decision.
issue.notes:
Investigation complete: This bead is already fully implemented. 

**Completed:** 2026-08-20 (commit 8a8e8f77) - 6 days after bead creation

**Implementation Summary:**
- Push subscriptions DB: Lazy initialization with retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff)
- Non-fatal startup: Server logs errors, continues in degraded mode
- Health endpoint: Reports pushDb status (ready/degraded)
- All DB-dependent routes return 503 when DB unavailable
- Core routes (arrivals, stations, routes, alerts, commute) remain functional

**Alert History:**
- No separate alert history SQLite database exists
- Alerts are stored in-memory only in delay-detector.ts
- Task description mentioned 'alert-history equivalent' but this subsystem doesn't use DB

**Verification:**
- Integration tests: packages/server/src/integration/database-failure.test.ts
- All routes check isPushDatabaseReady() before DB access
- CORE_ONLY mode support for future ADR-001 deployment split

This implementation matches ADR-001's 'incremental first step' (make SQLite opens lazy/best-effort before full manifest split).
issue.title: Make push-subscription and alert-history SQLite opens lazy/best-effort

issue.description:
## Task
Research and document the standard directory structure where NixOS installs system binaries.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Document the purpose of /run/current-system/sw/bin/ on NixOS
- Identify other common NixOS binary paths (e.g., /nix/var/nix/profiles/system/sw/bin/)
- Record findings in this bead's notes

## Notes
This is foundational research - understand where NixOS puts binaries before researching ripgrep specifically.
issue.notes:
## Findings

### /run/current-system/sw/bin/
- **Purpose**: Runtime symlink to current system generation's binaries
- **Created**: At boot time
- **Recommended for**: Scripts and PATH configuration
- **Stability**: More stable, always available at runtime

### /nix/var/nix/profiles/system/sw/bin/
- **Purpose**: System profile tracking system-wide package generations
- **Created**: Each time you run `nixos-rebuild switch`
- **Management**: The `system` symlink points to current generation
- **Generations**: Older ones stored as `system-N-link` (e.g., system-29-link, system-30-link)
- **List generations**: `sudo nix-env -p /nix/var/nix/profiles/system --list-generations`

### Directory Structure Chain
``
/run/current-system → /nix/var/nix/profiles/system → /nix/store/[hash]-system
``

Both paths ultimately point to the same location in the Nix store through symlinks.

### The 'sw' Directory
Contains:
- `bin/` - Executable binaries
- `share/` - Shared files (man pages, completions, etc.)
- `lib/` - Libraries

### Traditional Linux Equivalent
- **Traditional**: /usr/bin
- **NixOS**: /run/current-system/sw/bin or /nix/var/nix/profiles/system/sw/bin

Full documentation saved to: docs/research/nixos-binary-directory-structure.md
issue.title: Research NixOS system binary directory structure

issue.notes:
# Middleware Index File Contents

## File Location
packages/server/src/middleware/index.ts

## File Structure
The file is a barrel export that re-exports from ~30 different middleware modules, covering a comprehensive security and functionality stack.

## Export Pattern
All exports follow the pattern:
export { items } from './module-name.js';

## Module Categories (586 total exports)

### Core Middleware
- requestId
- rateLimiter
- cors
- requestSizeLimits

### Security Headers & CSP
- securityHeaders, generateCspNonce, getDefaultCsp, getStrictCsp

### Input Validation & Sanitization
- validateBody, validateQuery, validateParams
- inputSanitization, getSanitizedQuery
- pathTraversalPrevention, isSafePath
- massAssignmentProtection (with field constants)
- validateContentType, requireJson, requireFormData

### HTTP Security
- hppProtection (HTTP Parameter Pollution)
- jsonDepthProtection
- httpResponseSplitting
- httpRequestSmuggling (strict variant)
- httpMethodRestrictions

### Authentication & Authorization
- Full auth stack (apiKeyAuth, signedRequestAuth, optionalAuth, etc.)
- RBAC system (requirePermission, requireRole, etc.)
- Enhanced authorization (resource-based)
- Dynamic RBAC caching
- Password management

### Session Management
- sessionSecurity
- concurrent-session-management
- cookie security and signing
- token encryption/decryption

### Protection Mechanisms
- CSRF protection
- SSRF protection
- Open redirect protection
- Host header protection
- JWT validation with replay detection
- Enhanced JWT security with compromise detection

### Caching (9 strategies)
- staticCache, semiStaticCache, realtimeCache, apiCache, healthCache, noCache, noStore, etagCache, conditionalGet, immutableCache

### Audit & Monitoring
- securityLogger, securityLogging
- Audit logging (basic and structured)
- Security event notifications
- Dependency security checks

### Admin & Operations
- Admin operations (requireAdminWithAudit, etc.)
- API key management

### Rate Limiting
- authRateLimit (with IP ban/trusted IP support)

### Advanced Features
- CAPTCHA integration
- Time-based and location-based access control
- Behavioral analysis
- Subresource integrity (SRI)
- Response size limits

## Key Observations
1. Extensive security coverage - The middleware stack addresses OWASP Top 10 and many additional security concerns
2. Type exports included - Many modules export TypeScript types alongside functions
3. Dual naming pattern - Some exports have aliases (e.g., type PermissionAction as RbacPermissionAction)
4. Feature constants - Field whitelists exported as constants (e.g., PUSH_SUBSCRIPTION_FIELDS, TRIP_NOTES_FIELDS)
5. Utility functions - Many modules export helper functions alongside middleware
6. Configuration types - Most security middleware exports Options/Config types

## Next Step
Analyze the export pattern to understand the middleware architecture and determine if reorganization is needed.
issue.title: Read middleware index file

## What
Obtain gtfs-realtime.proto and nyct-subway.proto, compile them into a JavaScript module using protobufjs.

## Why
MTA feeds return binary protobuf, not JSON. The NYCT extensions (direction, is_assigned, train_id, scheduled_track, actual_track, trip_replacement_period) are critical for confidence scoring, reroute detection, and cancelled trip detection. Without the compiled proto, we can only parse base GTFS-RT fields.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Obtain gtfs-realtime.proto from MobilityData/gtfs-realtime-bindings
- [ ] Obtain nyct-subway.proto from MTA developer resources
- [ ] Compile both into packages/server/src/proto/compiled.js using protobufjs CLI (pbjs)
- [ ] Generate TypeScript definitions (pbts) for type safety
- [ ] Verify parsing of a sample MTA feed response
- [ ] Add npm script: `npm run compile-proto` in packages/server

## Considerations
- nyct-subway.proto extends the base GTFS-RT message types with MTA-specific fields
- The compiled output should be checked into git (not generated at build time) to avoid protobufjs as a build dependency
- Test with a real downloaded feed binary to catch extension parsing issues early
issue.title: Protobuf compilation: GTFS-RT + NYCT extensions

## What
Create all Zustand stores with localStorage persistence, versioned migration support, and backup safety.

## Why
This implements the data migration strategy (Section 14 of plan) from the start, not as a retrofit. Every store created from day one uses versioned persist, so schema evolution is safe throughout the entire project lifecycle.

## Subtasks
- [ ] favoritesStore: Favorite[], Commute[], tapHistory[], with persist v1
- [ ] settingsStore: theme, refreshInterval, showUnassignedTrips, accessibleMode, etc.
- [ ] arrivalsStore: cached StationArrivals per stationId (in-memory, not persisted — refresh from API)
- [ ] Migration infrastructure: backup key before migration, restore on failure, Sentry error logging
- [ ] Skeleton journalStore and fareStore (Phase 5-6, but version 1 schema defined now)

## Considerations
- Zustand persist middleware's version + migrate options handle the chain
- Backup key format: _mta_backup_{storeName}_v{version}
- tapHistory capped at 500 entries FIFO — must enforce on every append
- arrivalsStore is NOT persisted (it's a cache, refreshed every 30s) — but last-known values should be written to localStorage separately for offline mode
issue.title: Frontend: Zustand stores with versioned persistence

issue.close_reason:
Implemented weekly in-server GTFS static data refresh scheduler. All work committed in fa7e3a9.

- packages/server/src/gtfs-refresh.ts: new module with startGtfsRefreshScheduler() that uses setInterval (7-day interval), reentrancy guard (isRefreshing flag), structured logging via logger.info/error, spawns process-gtfs.mjs as a child process
- packages/server/src/index.ts: calls startGtfsRefreshScheduler() at startup alongside existing pollers
- Dockerfile: adds unzip system package to runtime stage, copies packages/server/scripts/ so the refresh script is available in the container
- packages/server/package.json: moves csv-parse from devDependencies to dependencies (required at runtime for process-gtfs.mjs)

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** setInterval-in-server approach fit naturally alongside existing equipment/delay pollers — same pattern, same logger, minimal code
- **What didn't:** N/A — straightforward implementation with no blockers
- **Surprise:** csv-parse was installed as a devDependency only; it needed promotion to production dependency since process-gtfs.mjs runs in the live container, not at build time
- **Reusable pattern:** For any periodic background task in this server, create src/<name>.ts with a start<Name>Scheduler() export wrapping setInterval with reentrancy guard and structured logger, then wire it in index.ts alongside the other pollers
issue.description: Plan Phase 1 specifies: GTFS static data pipeline — Script to download, parse, and pre-process stops.txt, routes.txt, and transfers.txt into optimized JSON. Run periodically (weekly cron) or manually when MTA updates schedules. The process-gtfs.mjs script exists and works, but there is no automation — no Kubernetes CronJob, no CI workflow, and no scheduled trigger. The static JSON files in packages/server/data/ are only updated when a developer runs the script manually. Per CLAUDE.md, no K8s Jobs/CronJobs — use long-running Deployments with internal scheduling.

## Test Research Complete

### Testing Framework
Vitest (v4.1.11 in root, v3.2.7 in packages)
- Multi-level configuration with root orchestrator
- Configuration files at vitest.config.ts and packages/*/vitest.config.ts

### Naming Convention
- Pattern: *.test.ts for TypeScript, *.test.tsx for React components
- Location: Co-located with source files
- Integration tests in /integration/ (server), E2E in /tests/e2e/

### Test Distribution
- 242 total test files across the monorepo
- Server: 133 tests (92 unit, 41 integration)
- Web: 61 tests (React components + hooks)
- Shared: 24 tests (utilities + schemas)
- E2E: 17 end-to-end tests

### Standard Imports
Unit tests: import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
React tests: import { render, screen } from "@testing-library/react";

### Test Structure Pattern
describe blocks for grouping, beforeEach hooks for setup, clear test names

### Mock Strategy
vi.mock() for module mocking (hoisted), vi.fn() for functions
Cleanup: beforeEach vi.clearAllMocks(), afterEach vi.restoreAllMocks()

### Test Environment
- Server: Node environment, fork pool (max 4 workers)
- Web: jsdom with React Testing Library + jest-dom matchers
- Coverage: V8 provider with text/json/html reporters

### Reference Files Analyzed
1. packages/server/src/cache.test.ts - Unit tests with describe blocks
2. packages/server/src/app.test.ts - Integration tests with fixtures
3. tests/directory.test.ts - Filesystem tests
4. packages/web/src/components/arrivals/LineBullet.test.tsx - React patterns

All tests and lint pass successfully.

issue.description:
## Problem

`npm test` runs vitest across 3 workspace packages (web, shared, server). With no config, vitest spawns workers equal to CPU count — on this 8-core box that's 20+ forked processes consuming ~1100% CPU and pushing load to 40+. Watch mode keeps them alive indefinitely.

## Fix

1. **Add `vitest.config.ts`** at root (or per-workspace) with:
   ```ts
   export default defineConfig({
     test: {
       pool: 'forks',
       poolOptions: { forks: { maxForks: 4 } },
     },
   })
   ```
2. **Change `test` script** in root `package.json` from `npm run test --workspaces` to include `--run` flag so it exits after one pass instead of watching
3. **Add a separate `test:watch` script** for intentional watch-mode usage

## Fallback

If local test runs are still too heavy, move the full suite to CI (`mta-my-way-build` workflow on iad-ci) and keep local `npm test` as a smoke test only.

## Context

- Vitest 3.2.4, 3 workspace packages (packages/web, packages/shared, packages/server)
- This is a shared Hetzner box — one dev's test run shouldn't cripple everything else
issue.title: Cap vitest worker count — max 4 workers, no watch mode by default

issue.description:
docs/authorization-audit.md and plan.md's "Shipped Architecture
Deviations" section (docs/plan/plan.md) document a comprehensive,
mostly-built auth framework -- API key auth (PBKDF2, 600k iterations),
session management (IP binding, device tracking, CSRF, sliding
expiration), OAuth 2.0 with PKCE (Google/GitHub), TOTP MFA -- that is
almost entirely disabled in app.ts. Only the credential-reset flow is
live. This is a large amount of already-implemented, already-audited
infrastructure sitting unused.

Favorites and commutes today are localStorage-only (see plan.md
Section 3.1, UserPreferences) -- they don't survive a new device or a
cleared browser. Wiring the existing (disabled) session middleware to
a simple GET/PUT /api/preferences endpoint, gated behind opt-in sign-in
(no forced account creation, matching the "no accounts required for
core features" promise in plan.md Section 1), would ship one of the
most commonly requested feature classes for a commuter PWA (use it on
phone + tablet, survive a phone swap) largely by turning on code that
already exists and has already been through a security audit, rather
than building new auth from scratch.

Do this after (or alongside) ADR-001's core/stateful split
(docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001, 2026-07-20) -- once auth/session state
can no longer take the core arrivals path down with it, it's safer to
depend on it for an opt-in feature.

Scope for a first pass: enable the existing session + OAuth routes for
sign-in only, add one new endpoint pair (get/put synced preferences),
and a client-side "Sign in to sync across devices" entry point in
settings. Leave MFA, API keys, and admin routes disabled -- out of
scope for this bead.
issue.title: Ship cross-device favorites sync using the existing (disabled) OAuth/session framework

## What
API endpoints for station search and serving pre-processed GTFS static data. These serve the frontend's search, station detail, and commute configuration features.

## Subtasks
- [ ] GET /api/stations — return full station index (from stations.json), cached aggressively
- [ ] GET /api/stations/:id — return single station with complex-aware expansion (all stations in same complex)
- [ ] GET /api/stations/search?q=... — type-ahead search by name, line, or cross-street
- [ ] GET /api/routes — return route index
- [ ] GET /api/static/complexes — return complexes.json
- [ ] Cache-Control headers: max-age=86400 for static data (changes only a few times per year)
- [ ] Complex-aware station lookup: when querying a station, include all lines across the complex

## Considerations
- Search should be fast (in-memory, not SQLite) since station count is only 472
- Search should handle common abbreviations: "Times Sq", "42 St", "B'way"
- Complex expansion is critical — searching "Times Square" must show 1/2/3/7/N/Q/R/W/S
issue.title: Backend: station search and static data API

issue.description:
## Goal
Production-quality app that is fast, accessible, and reliable even underground with no signal.

## Why This Matters
Subway commuters are underground most of their transit time. An app that breaks offline is useless exactly when it's needed most. Accessibility is non-negotiable for a public transit app — wheelchair users, visually impaired riders, and elderly commuters all depend on transit.

## Key Decisions
- WCAG 2.1 AA minimum compliance (not just aspirational — tested)
- Lighthouse targets: Performance 95+, Accessibility 100, Best Practices 100, PWA 100
- Stale data detection via VehiclePosition timestamps
- DataState wrapper component enforces 6 states on all data views (Section 13 of plan)
- Bundle size budget enforced in CI

## Acceptance Criteria
- Offline mode shows cached data with staleness indicator
- WCAG 2.1 AA compliance verified by automated and manual testing
- Screen reader tested on VoiceOver (iOS) and TalkBack (Android)
- First Contentful Paint under 1.5s on 3G
- All data views handle loading/loaded/empty/error/stale/offline states via DataState

## Dependencies
- Requires Phases 1-3 features to be functional (this phase polishes them)
issue.title: Phase 4: Polish — Offline, Accessibility, Performance

issue.notes:
Main Entry Point Analysis

File: packages/server/src/index.ts

Startup Sequence (documented in file comments, lines 1-10):
1. Load GTFS static data (stations, routes, complexes, transfers, travel times)
2. Create Hono app (also builds TransferEngine internally)
3. Initialize push notification subsystem (SQLite DB, VAPID keys, pipeline)
4. Start HTTP server (health endpoint becomes available immediately)
5. Start feed pollers in background (first poll fires immediately but async)

createApp() Call (line 138):
- Parameters: stations, routes, complexes, transfers, WEB_DIST
- Import location: ./app.js (line 24)
- All parameters loaded from JSON files in data/ directory

Key Initialization Details:
- Security validation happens early (line 63) - fail-fast pattern
- Observability (OTel, tracing, metrics) initialized before anything else (line 60)
- Rate limiter test mode via TEST_MODE env var (lines 84-89)
- CORE_ONLY mode skips all DB-dependent subsystems (lines 142-172)
- HTTP server starts BEFORE pollers (line 179) - ensures health endpoint available immediately
- Graceful shutdown handlers registered (lines 197-218)

Next Step Context:
The createApp() function (imported from ./app.js) is where middleware registration happens. This is the logical next place to examine middleware organization.
issue.title: Examine main application entry point

issue.description:
## Task
Research and compare the two candidate WebSearch query options for finding NixOS official documentation.

## Candidate Queries
1. "NixOS official manual"
2. "NixOS documentation"

## Acceptance Criteria
- Document what each query would likely return
- Identify which query is more precise and comprehensive
- Note any official NixOS documentation URLs discovered

## Deliverable
Add notes to this bead comparing the two options with a recommendation.
issue.notes:
## WebSearch Query Comparison for NixOS Documentation

### Query 1: "NixOS official manual"
**What it returns:**
- **Primary:** NixOS Manual (https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/)
- Learn Nix portal (https://nixos.org/learn/)
- NixOS Wiki (https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/NixOS_Wiki)
- Nixpkgs Reference Manual (https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/manual/)
- Main NixOS website (https://nixos.org/)
- NixOS Installation Guide (https://nixos.wiki/wiki/NixOS_Installation_Guide)

**Characteristics:** Highly focused on the manual and official resources. The word "official" and "manual" make this query very specific.

### Query 2: "NixOS documentation"
**What it returns:**
- **Primary:** NixOS Manual (https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/)
- All resources from Query 1, plus:
- Nix reference manual (https://nix.dev/reference/nix-manual.html) - Additional official resource
- Community GitHub guide (https://github.com/mikeroyal/NixOS-Guide)
- Download page (https://nixos.org/download/)
- Official GitHub repos (https://github.com/nixos)

**Characteristics:** Broader scope while still maintaining precision. Captures both the manual and related documentation resources.

## Comparison Summary

| Aspect | Query 1 ("NixOS official manual") | Query 2 ("NixOS documentation") |
|--------|-------------------------------------|-----------------------------------|
| Primary Result | NixOS Manual ✓ | NixOS Manual ✓ |
| Official Coverage | Excellent | Excellent+ |
| Community Resources | Minimal | Includes guides |
| Natural Language | Slightly formal | More natural |
| Breadth | Focused | Comprehensive |

## Recommendation

**Use "NixOS documentation"**

**Rationale:**
1. Both queries correctly identify the NixOS Manual as the primary resource
2. Query 2 provides slightly broader coverage including the Nix reference manual (nix.dev)
3. The query is shorter, more natural, and less redundant
4. "Documentation" is a more inclusive term that captures manuals, guides, wikis, and references

**Key Official URLs Discovered:**
- **Primary:** https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/ (NixOS Manual - the authoritative source)
- **Learning:** https://nixos.org/learn/ (Official learning portal)
- **Reference:** https://nixos.org/nixpkgs/manual/ (Nixpkgs manual)
- **Wiki:** https://wiki.nixos.org/wiki/NixOS_Wiki (Official community wiki)
- **Nix Reference:** https://nix.dev/reference/nix-manual.html (Nix package manager docs)

Both queries are effective and would serve the purpose well, but "NixOS documentation" has a slight edge in comprehensiveness and natural language usage.
issue.title: Research NixOS documentation search query options

issue.description:
## Evidence
plan.md Phase 5 feature 3 ('Time-aware context switching') specifies: 'Implementation: Entirely client-side using localStorage.' plan.md Section 12.3 (Data Privacy) states: 'No PII stored server-side. Favorites, commute journal, fare tracking, tap history — all localStorage, never sent to the backend.'

However packages/server/src/context-service.ts implements a full server-side context detection/persistence service (detectAndUpdateContextWithOwner, recordContextDetection, recordContextOverride, getContextTransitionsForOwner, etc.), backed by user_context and context_transitions SQLite tables created in packages/server/src/migration/migrations/016-add-trips-table.ts (lines ~60-90). This is exposed via live, mounted routes: app.use("/api/context/*", requireSameOrigin()) and app.get("/api/context", ...) in packages/server/src/app.ts (~line 2300).

Grepping the entire packages/web/src frontend for any call to /api/context returns zero matches as of this audit. The frontend's packages/web/src/stores/contextStore.ts implements context switching entirely client-side, exactly as the plan describes, and never calls this server API. The server-side context feature therefore appears to be dead code that was built in parallel with (not integrated into) the actual shipped client-side implementation, and that also stores tap/usage-pattern data server-side in contradiction of the plan's explicit no-PII-server-side promise.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Re-confirm (grep packages/web/src for /api/context, context-service, and any fetch/axios call referencing context) that no frontend code path calls this API before acting — if a caller is found, this bead's premise is wrong; document that and close without further action
- If confirmed unused, resolve the contradiction via ONE of:
  (a) Remove the unused server-side context feature: packages/server/src/context-service.ts, its /api/context* route mounts in app.ts, and the associated request schemas/imports, plus a plan for the now-unused user_context/context_transitions tables (a down-migration, or explicitly marking them deprecated-but-retained with a comment, whichever is lower-risk) — restoring alignment with plan.md's stated client-side design and privacy promise, OR
  (b) If there's a concrete near-term plan to wire the frontend to this API, add a 'Shipped Architecture Deviations' entry to plan.md Section 16 (alongside the existing auth-framework and map-screen entries) documenting why server-side context storage exists despite the stated client-side/no-PII design
- No change to the frontend's existing client-side contextStore.ts behavior is required under either path
issue.notes:
Verification complete: This issue was already resolved in August 2026. 

Confirmed:
- Frontend packages/web/src/ has ZERO calls to /api/context, context-service, or any fetch/axios context APIs (grep verified)
- Server-side packages/server/src/context-service.ts does NOT exist (deleted)
- Plan.md Section 16.6 already documents the resolution: 'Server-side context storage removed to align with client-side design'
- Database tables (user_context, context_transitions) exist only as DEPRECATED for backward compatibility per migration 016 comments

The premise of this bead was correct, but the work was already completed prior to this bead being claimed. Resolution path (a) was chosen: remove the unused server-side context feature, restoring alignment with plan.md's client-side/no-PII design.
issue.title: Resolve unused server-side /api/context feature (contradicts plan's client-side-only design and privacy promise)

issue.description:
## Goal
Build user trust through data transparency and provide critical fallback information when the system breaks down.

## Why This Matters
The worst moment for a commuter is when their line is suspended. The MTA says "use shuttle bus" but never says WHERE. And users need to know how fresh the data they're seeing actually is — especially given the A Division vs B Division accuracy gap.

## Key Decisions
- Shuttle bus stops are a curated static JSON lookup (not dynamic — MTA doesn't provide this data electronically)
- Start with 10 most common suspension segments, grow incrementally
- Data freshness shows per-feed age with color coding: green <15s, amber 45-90s, red >90s
- Per-arrival feedName field lets frontend show which feed each arrival came from

## Acceptance Criteria
- Shuttle bus info displayed for 10+ common suspension segments
- Data freshness visible on all station detail views with color-coded staleness

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 3 (alert parsing for NO_SERVICE detection)
- Requires Phase 1 (feed pipeline with per-feed timestamps)
issue.title: Phase 7: Trust & Resilience — Shuttle Info, Data Freshness

The proto compiled types include TripReplacementPeriod but parser.ts and transformer.ts do not use it. No code in the server references trip_replacement_period for cancelled trip logic. Need to: (1) extract trip_replacement_period from the NYCT feed header in parser.ts, (2) cross-reference absent tripIds against the replacement window in transformer.ts, (3) emit a synthetic Cancelled arrival entry in the StationArrivals response, (4) display it in ArrivalRow with a struck-through or dimmed visual.

issue.description:
## Goal
Transform the app from a data display into a predictive, context-aware commute companion that learns and anticipates.

## Why This Matters
This is where the app becomes genuinely differentiated. No competitor predicts delays before the MTA announces them, no competitor tracks your trip and shares ETA, no competitor learns your patterns to auto-sort favorites, and no competitor builds a personal commute history.

## Key Decisions
- Predictive delay detection: diff VehiclePosition across polls, compare vs scheduled inter-station times
- Trip tracking locks onto a specific tripId in the GTFS-RT feed
- Time-aware context switching is 100% client-side (localStorage tapHistory)
- Smart pre-fetch uses Geolocation API (only works when app is open — acceptable)
- Commute journal infers trips from app usage patterns (no always-on required)
- OMNY fare cap auto-logged from trip data (no manual button)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Predictive delay warnings fire 5-10 min before official MTA alerts for detectable slowdowns
- Live trip tracking with shareable ETA link working
- Context-aware favorite sorting active after 2 weeks of usage
- Offline countdown working underground with cached data
- Commute journal logging trips and surfacing anomalies

## Dependencies
- Requires Phase 1-2 (backend feed pipeline, transfer engine, station data)
- Requires Phase 3 (push infrastructure for morning briefing notifications)
issue.title: Phase 5: Intelligence — Predictive Delays, Trip Tracking, Learning

issue.notes:
## Research Findings: NixOS ripgrep Binary Path

### Standard NixOS Path
The standard path where ripgrep (rg) is installed on NixOS systems is:

**/run/current-system/sw/bin/rg**

### Verification
- `which rg` → /run/current-system/sw/bin/rg
- `command -v rg` → /run/current-system/sw/bin/rg
- Confirmed on NixOS 26.05

### Path Structure
`/run/current-system/sw/bin/rg` is a symlink to the actual binary in the Nix store:
- Symlink: /run/current-system/sw/bin/rg
- Target: /nix/store/<hash>-ripgrep-15.1.0/bin/rg

### Other NixOS Binary Locations (Not Applicable for ripgrep)
- ~/.nix-profile/bin/ - User-specific packages (not present)
- /etc/profiles/per-user/<user>/bin/ - User profile binaries (not present)

### Recommendation
Use `/run/current-system/sw/bin/rg` as the standard NixOS ripgrep path. This path:
- Is stable across NixOS installations
- Is automatically updated when the system configuration changes
- Follows the NixOS convention of symlinking /run/current-system/sw/ to the active system generation
issue.title: Determine NixOS ripgrep binary path

Implements the manifest-level half of ADR-001 (docs/plan/plan.md,
2026-07-20). Today's deployment.yaml (in declarative-config, path:
k8s / apexalgo-iad / mta-my-way) runs one container, replicas: 1,
strategy Recreate, with a required PVC volumeMount at /data. A CSI
mount failure on that PVC (confirmed live 2026-07-20: pod stuck
ContainerCreating for 9+ hours, FailedMount x292) takes down the
entire app, including the fully in-memory arrivals/stations/alerts/PWA
path that needs zero persistence.

Work:
1. Add a CORE_ONLY env var / startup flag to the server (packages/server)
   that skips mounting push/auth/password-reset routes and skips
   opening any SQLite database.
2. In declarative-config, add a second Deployment + Service (e.g.
   mta-my-way-core) running the image with CORE_ONLY=true, no PVC,
   replicas: 2, strategy RollingUpdate.
3. Point the existing IngressRoute (mtamyway.com) at the new core
   Service for all paths except the push/auth/password-reset routes,
   which continue to route to the existing single-replica stateful
   Deployment.
4. Core calls the stateful subsystem's ClusterIP Service with a short
   timeout + circuit breaker for anything push/auth related; on
   failure it degrades that feature only.

This is the larger follow-up to bf-20agd (image pinning) and the lazy
DB-open bead -- do the lazy-open change first since it's a much
smaller, faster-to-ship risk reduction, then this split for the full
fix.

issue.description:
The audit log bridge middleware in `packages/server/src/integration/audit-log-security-events.test.ts` cannot capture events when `hostHeaderProtection` blocks a request because it short-circuits (returns early without calling `await next()`).

The `createHostHeaderAuditApp` factory (lines 202-214) places `hostHeaderProtection` BEFORE the `auditLogBridgeMiddleware`. When hostHeaderProtection blocks, the bridge middleware never executes.

Fix approach: Modify `createHostHeaderAuditApp` to add an `addAuditEvent` call directly inside a wrapper around hostHeaderProtection, OR restructure the factory so that the host-header middleware calls `addAuditEvent` before returning the 400 response. The simplest approach is to wrap hostHeaderProtection in a custom middleware that intercepts the 400 response and writes the audit event.

Acceptance criteria:
- Host-header protection blocks now produce audit log entries with category=security
- Audit entries contain correct metadata (IP, path, method, timestamp)
- Other host-header tests (allowed host, IP in Host header, timestamp check) continue to work
- No changes to production middleware code — only test infrastructure

## What
Build the transfer analysis engine that computes multi-leg routes from real-time arrival data for a given origin/destination pair.

## Subtasks
- [ ] Station graph (graph.ts): build weighted graph from transfers.json + complexes.json
- [ ] Travel times (travel-times.ts): load scheduled inter-station times, index by route+direction
- [ ] Engine (engine.ts): for origin→destination, find all direct routes and transfer routes
- [ ] Direct route scoring: line + next arrival at origin + travel time to destination
- [ ] Transfer route scoring: first leg + walking time + wait at transfer + second leg travel time
- [ ] B Division buffer: add +2 min to B Division arrival estimates in transfer calculations
- [ ] Rank all routes by total estimated arrival time at destination
- [ ] Flag when transfer saves time vs direct: "Transfer saves X min" computation
- [ ] API route: POST /api/commute/analyze (origin, destination, preferred lines)

## Considerations
- Transfer routes are limited to 1 transfer (2 legs max) — 2+ transfers are rarely useful in NYC
- The graph must include complex-aware transfers (e.g., 1/2/3 → N/Q/R/W at Times Square)
- Walking time defaults to transfers.txt min_transfer_time, fallback 180s
- Express/local detection: compare a trip's stop_time_updates against the route's full stop list — missing stops = express

## Goal
Foundational infrastructure that spans all phases: testing strategy, security model, data migration, and observability. These are not features users see directly but they determine whether the app is trustworthy, maintainable, and operable.

## Why This Is Priority 1
These concerns must be addressed from the start, not retrofitted:
- Testing: feed snapshot fixtures must be recorded during Phase 1 development
- Security: rate limiting and CSP headers must be in place before public launch
- Data migration: Zustand versioned persist must be set up with the first store
- Observability: structured logging must be in the feed pipeline from day one

## Key Decisions
- No external monitoring infrastructure (no Prometheus, no Grafana) — structured JSON logs + rich /api/health endpoint
- Zod for all API input validation
- Cloudflare WAF + Hono token bucket for rate limiting (defense in depth)
- Feed snapshot testing with recorded binary fixtures (never depend on live MTA feeds in CI)
- Zustand's built-in version + migrate for localStorage schema evolution

## Acceptance Criteria
- Feed snapshot test fixtures recorded for all 8 feeds + alerts
- Unit, integration, and E2E test layers implemented and passing in CI
- Rate limiting active at both Cloudflare and application layers
- CSP headers served on all HTML responses
- Zod validation on all API endpoints
- Zustand stores use versioned persistence with backup migration safety
- /api/health returns comprehensive per-feed observability payload
- Structured JSON logging on every feed poll
issue.title: Cross-Cutting: Testing, Security, Migration, Observability

issue.notes: Verification-only audit completed; no source or documentation files were changed, staged, or committed. Auth inventory: packages/server/src/middleware/authentication.ts contains PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 API-key hashing at 600000 iterations, session creation/validation/refresh with CSRF token, device ID, IP binding, 30-minute idle timeout, 24-hour absolute lifetime, refresh-token rotation, OAuth PKCE state, and TOTP with backup codes and a plus-or-minus one 30-second verification window. middleware/csrf-protection.ts, authorization.ts, rbac.ts, cookie-security.ts, and session-security.ts provide CSRF, same-origin, RBAC/ownership, cookie, and enhanced session controls. session-security.ts is not wired into app.ts. API-key lifecycle code is in middleware/api-key-management.ts; persistence scaffolding is in security/security-db.ts and migration 018, but startup initialization is currently unwired. Ownership support is present in trip-tracking.ts and migration 017. The live credential-reset flow is routes/password-reset.routes.ts plus middleware/password-management.ts and services/password-reset.service.ts, with web reset screens/routes. Current app.ts has optional auth parsing and CSRF middleware, guarded trip/journal/commute/push routes, and live password reset/change routes. In the committed app baseline, OAuth routes, all MFA routes, and legacy session status/refresh/revoke routes are commented out. The shared working tree has concurrent uncommitted changes that currently uncomment OAuth Google/GitHub routes and add preferences plus session status/revoke routes; session refresh and MFA remain disabled. The audit document is therefore not accurate as a current snapshot: its PBKDF2, session-framework, PKCE/TOTP-library, and in-memory active-auth-state claims are broadly supported, but its claim that read/ownership protections are absent is stale; current app.ts uses RBAC/ownership guards and trip/push storage has owner_id. Context endpoints documented by the audit were removed and are client-side only. The OAuth working-tree implementation has PKCE/state and 10-minute state expiry but no nonce validation, its callback bypasses the separate state-validation helper, and it is not typecheck-clean. Sliding refresh exists as a library function but no active refresh route or middleware uses it. No HTTP API-key management routes, password login/registration, MFA routes, session refresh route, durable OAuth/session/TOTP storage, or context routes were found. Targeted npm run typecheck --workspace=@mta-my-way/server was run and failed due the concurrent in-flight changes, including OAuth/preferences errors and unrelated existing errors.
issue.title: Inventory and audit disabled auth framework

issue.description:
The live deployment.yaml pins the container to ronaldraygun/mta-my-way
with tag "latest" and imagePullPolicy Always (in the declarative-config
repo, path: k8s / apexalgo-iad / mta-my-way / deployment.yaml). This
violates the workspace CI policy ("Never use latest image tags --
always pin to a specific digest or version tag") and means ArgoCD and
kubectl cannot diff or roll back to a known-good image -- every push to
main silently rolls forward with no pinned prior state to revert to if
a build regresses.

Fix: have the mta-my-way image build template (declarative-config repo,
under k8s / iad-ci / argo-workflows) tag images with the git SHA (or the
semver from VERSION) in addition to "latest", and update deployment.yaml
in declarative-config to reference that pinned tag/digest instead of
"latest". Bump the pinned tag as part of the normal deploy flow
(commit, push, ArgoCD sync), same as any other manifest change.

Referenced in this repo's docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) as
follow-up work.
issue.notes:
Task already completed — verified 2026-08-26:

Original fix committed 2026-07-26 (716ebf62): pinned deployment from :latest to :0.0.82, added image tagging and auto-update workflow.

Deployment split committed 2026-08-07 (20f400c1): split into deployment-core.yaml and deployment-stateful.yaml, workflow updated to handle both.

Current state verified:
- Both deployments pinned to ronaldraygun/mta-my-way:0.0.83
- Both use imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
- Workflow tags images with :<version>, :sha-<commit>, :latest
- update-declarative-config step auto-updates both deployments on build

No changes needed — workspace CI policy already satisfied.
issue.title: Pin mta-my-way deployment image off :latest tag

issue.description:
Ensure the 'rejects unexpected query parameters' test correctly validates that extra params are rejected.

Context:
- The test sends /api/health?extra=param and expects 400 with an error property
- The health handler calls validateQuery(c, emptyQuerySchema) where emptyQuerySchema = z.object({}).strict()
- BEFORE validation, inputSanitization middleware runs and stores sanitized params via c.set('sanitizedQuery', ...)
- validateQuery prefers sanitizedQuery over raw query params
- If sanitization strips unknown params, the validation would see {} and PASS (returning 200) instead of FAILING (returning 400)

Scope:
- Verify inputSanitization middleware behavior: does it strip unknown query params or only sanitize values?
- If sanitization strips params, the test expectation is wrong OR the sanitization should preserve unknown params for the validation layer to reject
- Fix either the test, the middleware ordering, or the sanitization behavior
- Ensure the 400 response includes an 'error' property as the test expects

Acceptance criteria:
- /api/health?extra=param reliably returns 400
- Response body has an 'error' property
- The rejection happens through the proper validation chain (not a side effect)
issue.title: Fix query param rejection test against sanitization middleware

## Task
Research the fundamental concepts of NixOS system profiles and activation scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Understand what NixOS system profiles are
- Document how /run/current-system/ is created during system activation

- Record findings in this bead's notes

## Notes
This is child bead 1 of 4 for documenting /run/current-system/sw/bin/ purpose.
issue.notes:
## Research Findings: NixOS System Profiles and Activation Scripts

### What are NixOS System Profiles?

**System Profile Location:** `/nix/var/nix/profiles/system`

The system profile is a Nix profile that contains all system generations. Each generation represents a complete, immutable system configuration stored in the Nix store.

- Managed via `nix-env -p /nix/var/nix/profiles/system`
- Each generation is a store path containing the complete system configuration
- Systemd-boot iterates through all generations to configure boot entries
- Can roll back to previous generations via `nixos-rebuild switch --rollback` or GRUB

**System Profile Structure (this system):**
- Current profile: `/nix/var/nix/profiles/system -> system-17-link`
- Latest generation: `system-17-link -> /nix/store/57dd4gicqyhvfpqj3mmibgxpi89isgl4-nixos-system-codinghome-26.05.20260826.062346a`
- Previous generations: system-1-link through system-16-link

### How /run/current-system is Created

**Creation Mechanism:** Atomic symlink replacement during activation

From activation-script.nix (line 157):
```bash
ln -sfn "$(readlink -f "$systemConfig")" /run/current-system
```

**Purpose:**
- Represents the currently active system configuration
- Points to a store path in `/nix/store/` (the activated generation)
- Serves as a garbage collection root
- Provides access to system-wide packages via `/run/current-system/sw/bin/`

**Actual path on this system:**
```bash
/run/current-system -> /nix/store/57dd4gicqyhvfpqj3mmibgxpi89isgl4-nixos-system-codinghome-26.05.20260826.062346a
```

**Structure of /run/current-system:**
- `/activate` - Main activation script (5516 bytes, bash)
- `/dry-activate` - Test activation without making changes
- `/bin/` - Contains switch-to-configuration script
- `/sw` - **symlink to system packages** (`/nix/store/17n18lm73c7z2c076anllnknlfx4wqmy-system-path`) 
  - This is where `/run/current-system/sw/bin/` comes from
  - Contains: bin/, sbin/, lib/, share/, etc.
- `/init` - the init system (systemd or bootStage2)
- `/prepare-root` - root filesystem preparation (systemd-initrd)
- `/etc` - symlink to `/etc` configuration
- `/systemd` - systemd package
- `/kernel` - kernel bzImage
- `/initrd` - initramfs
- `/kernel-modules` - kernel modules
- `/firmware` - kernel firmware
- `/boot.json` - bootloader configuration
- `/nixos-version` - NixOS label (26.05.20260826.062346a)
- `/kernel-params` - kernel parameters (root=fstab loglevel=4 lsm=landlock,yama,bpf)

### Key Activation Scripts and Files

**1. /run/current-system/activate**
Main activation script that:
- Sets up /bin/sh symlink (snippet: binsh)
- Creates user accounts and groups (snippet: users)
- Mounts special filesystems (snippet: specialfs)
- Sets up /etc configuration (snippet: etc)
- Validates password hash algorithms (snippet: hashes)
- Configures kernel module loading (snippet: modprobe)
- Installs secrets via sops (snippet: setupSecrets)
- Configures udev and firmware paths (snippet: udevd)
- Creates /usr/bin/env symlink (snippet: usrbinenv)
- **Creates /run/current-system symlink** (line 157)

**2. /run/current-system/bin/switch-to-configuration**
Wrapper script that:
- Sets environment variables (OUT, TOPLEVEL, DISTRO_ID, etc.)
- Executes the wrapped switch-to-configuration binary
- Used by nixos-rebuild to activate new configurations

**3. system.build.toplevel (top-level.nix)**
- Path: `nixos/modules/system/activation/top-level.nix`
- Creates the system derivation via `pkgs.stdenvNoCC.mkDerivation`
- Generates a store path named: `nixos-system-${config.system.name}-${config.system.nixos.label}`
- Contains symlinks to kernel, systemd units, init scripts
- Includes the `switch-to-configuration` script

**4. activation-script.nix**
- Path: `nixos/modules/system/activation/activation-script.nix`
- Generates the main activation script
- Handles both normal and dry-activation modes
- Processes activation snippets in dependency order
- Creates `/run/current-system` atomically

### The Activation Process

Complete flow for `nixos-rebuild switch`:

1. **Build:** `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.mymachine.config.system.build.toplevel`
   - Evaluates configuration.nix
   - Builds the system derivation
   - Produces a store path (result)

2. **Set Profile:** `nix-env -p /nix/var/nix/profiles/system --set ./result`
   - Creates a new generation in the system profile
   - Makes the new generation the current profile

3. **Activate:** `./result/bin/switch-to-configuration switch`
   - Runs activation scripts
   - Creates `/run/current-system` symlink
   - Updates `/etc` configuration files
   - Restarts systemd services
   - Sets configuration as default boot target

### Key Configuration Files

- **`/etc/nixos/configuration.nix`** or **`/etc/nixos/flake.nix`** - System configuration
- **`nixos/modules/system/activation/top-level.nix`** - Builds system.toplevel
- **`nixos/modules/system/activation/activation-script.nix`** - Generates activation script
- **`nixos/modules/system/activation/activatable-system.nix`** - Activatable system logic

### Modern Developments

**Deprecation of Activation Scripts:**

issue.description:
## Task
Research and document the purpose and function of /run/current-system/sw/bin/ on NixOS.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Explain what /run/current-system/sw/bin/ is
- Document how it is created/populated
- Explain its relationship to the NixOS system profile
- Record findings in the parent bead's notes

## Context
This is child bead 1 of 3 for researching NixOS system binary directory structure.
issue.notes:
Research completed and documented.

## Key Findings

### What is /run/current-system/sw/bin?
- Runtime symlink to the current system generation's binaries
- Points to /nix/store/[hash]-system-path/bin/
- Every binary is a symlink to actual binaries in /nix/store/
- Volatile - created during nixos-rebuild, lost on reboot

### How it is created/populated
1. nixos-rebuild evaluates configuration.nix and NixOS modules
2. Collects all packages from environment.systemPackages
3. Builds a special 'system-path' store path that consolidates all packages
4. Updates /nix/var/nix/profiles/system (persistent profile)
5. Creates /run/current-system symlinks (volatile runtime path)

### Relationship to NixOS system profile
- /run/current-system = volatile, currently running system
- /nix/var/nix/profiles/system = persistent, all generations
- Both point to same Nix store generation when running
- System profile provides boot menu entries

### Documentation
Full findings documented in:
docs/research/nixos-binary-directory-structure.md

Verified on live NixOS 26.05.20260826.062346a system.
issue.title: Document /run/current-system/sw/bin purpose

issue.description:
## Evidence
docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20, "Decouple the Core Read Path from Persistent-Volume-Backed State") names an "incremental first step, deployable before the full manifest split": make the better-sqlite3 opens in packages/server/src/push/subscriptions.ts lazy/best-effort rather than a startup-blocking call in index.ts, "so an unwritable or corrupt /data doesn't crash process startup even in cases where the mount technically succeeds but the filesystem underneath is bad."

This has NOT been done. In packages/server/src/index.ts (~line 149-150):

  const pushDbPath = process.env["PUSH_DB_PATH"] ?? join(DATA_DIR, "subscriptions.db");
  initPushDatabase(pushDbPath);
  const pushDb = getPushDatabase();

initPushDatabase() (packages/server/src/push/subscriptions.ts) calls `new Database(dbPath)` directly with no try/catch. This whole block runs before the HTTP server starts listening, so any exception here still crashes the entire process before /api/health, /api/arrivals, /api/stations etc. can ever come up — i.e. the exact single-point-of-failure ADR-001 is meant to eliminate is still fully present in code, even though the plan document already claims this was addressed.

Correction to ADR-001's own description while investigating this: the ADR and notes/bf-2uz2z.md both refer to a second SQLite file "alert_history.db" / env var ALERT_HISTORY_PATH for alert history, backed by its own db open. Repo-wide search (git log --all and grep across packages/server/src) turns up zero references to ALERT_HISTORY_PATH or an alert-history db file anywhere in actual code — only in the plan/notes prose. README's Project Structure section confirms there is only one SQLite file in packages/server/data (subscriptions, trips, sessions all in the same db opened via initPushDatabase/getPushDatabase). Scope this bead to that single db; if a genuinely separate alert-history store is later intended, note that as a documentation follow-up rather than assuming it already exists.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Wrap the initPushDatabase() call path (or the module-level open in subscriptions.ts) so a failure to open/init the db (corrupt file, EIO, read-only fs) is caught and logged, not thrown to the top of index.ts's startup sequence
- On failure, the process continues starting: HTTP server binds and listens, and stateless/read-only endpoints (/api/health, /api/arrivals/*, /api/stations, /api/routes, /api/alerts, /api/commute/analyze, static PWA assets) keep working
- Endpoints that require the db (push subscribe, trip tracking, sessions, password-reset, security persistence) degrade gracefully — return a clear 503/"degraded" rather than crashing the process — when the db failed to open
- /api/health reports the push/db subsystem as degraded (not overall service failure) when this happens
- Add or update a test that simulates an unopenable db path and asserts the server still starts and /api/health responds
- Correct the "alert_history.db" / ALERT_HISTORY_PATH references in docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 and notes/bf-2uz2z.md to reflect that there is one db file, not two (small doc fix, can be folded into this bead or split into a docs-only follow-up comment)
